releaseNotes: NChat 1.0.58 — notifications while the app is closed, without Google. On Android the only channel that can wake an app on Google's behalf is Firebase, and this app deliberately has none of it. So NChat keeps its own connection instead: a foreground service holds the realtime socket the UI already uses, which means the existing notification code fires while the app is gone — sender name, message text, inline reply, tap opens that chat. No second transport, no push server, no Firebase, no per-message cost. There is one visible price, and it is the honest one: a quiet NChat line in the notification shade (Android requires it for a foreground service), collapsed at the bottom and silent, plus a small battery cost. Settings ▸ Notifications has a new switch for it and a Battery usage row that asks Android to leave NChat awake. Turning it off changes nothing else — messages simply wait until you open the app.
